summary: 1934 steel lookout tower on Blue Ridge, Klamath National Forest, Siskiyou County; NHLR-registered 1995; 2020 Register visit found it unstaffed and in poor condition.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab per the Register; a 1952 survey describes a four-legged steel tower with a 10 foot square metal house on top
facts.status_note: Standing, but the October 2020 Register visit found the wood, stairs and glass not in good order and the tower needing paint

visit.trail_note: Road-trip guide: the summit road is unpaved and needs a 4x4; the 2020 Register visit found no sign and no signed directions to the tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register describes 80 foot Aermotor towers; the 1952 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives a 110 foot four-legged steel tower. Facts keep 33.5 m (110 ft) from the survey, which matches the record. The Register figure would be about 24.4 m. Not resolved.
Register gives 7 by 7 foot cabs; the 1952 survey gives a 10 foot square metal house. Not resolved.

Register description and the road guide say the tower is still staffed each year. The Register's own visit reports (September 4, 2004 and October 21, 2020) both record Staffed? No. The 2020 visit was in October, after the usual season; the description is undated. Facts record unstaffed as of the 2020 visit only.

notes_for_editor: The Register's 'still staffed each year' wording is repeated by dangerousroads.org, so it is not independent confirmation; the Register's own visit reports point the other way. No 2025 or 2026 source on current staffing or access was found. The summit road description comes from a road-trip site, not a land manager. A Scott Valley News Facebook post about the tower was not readable (login wall). A SummitPost entry for a Blue Ridge in Tulare County (1930, 60 ft) is a different tower and was not used. Our record's height 33.5 m matches the 1952 survey, not the Register's 80 ft. No photos added; the Register page carries captions only, with no image URLs.
